requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** The implementation matches every obligation, the selector spelling is documented, and the tests cover the design space. The only gaps are minor and don't change the verdict.

**Implementation (`src/outline/rust.rs`)**
- `KINDS` maps the required Rust items to outline kinds:
  - functions and trait method signatures (`function_item`, `function_signature_item`) to `fn`
  - `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item` and `mod_item` to `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` and `mod`
  - `impl_item` to `impl`
  - `macro_definition` to `macro`, named by `name`
  - item-position `macro_invocation` to `macro`, anonymous
  - `const_item`, `static_item` and `type_item` to `const`, `static` and `type`
  - `associated_type` to `type`
  - `foreign_mod_item` to `extern`
  - `extern_crate_declaration` to `extern-crate`
  - `use_declaration` to `use`, anonymous
- Named kinds take their name from the `name` field, which gives `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]`. Nesting comes from the generic outline tree, so `fn[outer]/fn[inner]` falls out. That generic code is covered by `outline_selectors`.
- `impl_name` names an impl by its syntactic self type, plus the trait path when present. This gives `impl[Thing]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]` and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- `item_macro` and `in_item_list` keep expression-position macros out of the outline and make item-position macros anonymous.
- `extern_name` names an extern block by its ABI string, or `Rust` when there is none. The requirement doesn't spell this out, but it follows from "extern blocks MUST be outline nodes", and it is documented and tested.
- Nothing resolves modules across files. A `mod external;` is just `mod[external]`.
- `PROFILE` carries the `{impl}` references for the profile as a whole. The helper functions carry their own `{impl}` references.
- Selector spelling is documented in `md/reference.md`:
  - "Rust items" gives the examples, the impl naming, the anonymous `use` and macro cases, and the "never resolved across files" rule.
  - "Outline profiles" has a Rust table listing every kind, its grammar nodes and its naming rule.

**Tests (`src/outline/tests.rs`)**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` covers every required kind. It asserts:
  - `mod[local]/fn[run]`
  - `mod[external]`
  - `struct[Thing]`
  - `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`
  - `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`
  - an impl on `[u8; 4]`, percent-encoded
  - a trait method and `type[Item]`
  - `extern[C]/fn[puts]` and `extern[Rust]/fn[other]`
  - `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`
  - duplicate `#1` and `#2` selectors
  - `macro[make]`, `union`, `enum`, `const`, `static`, `type` and `extern-crate`
  - Each selector also round-trips through `resolve`, the empty selector resolves to the root, and ambiguous or missing selectors fail.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` repeats the main cases and asserts that `use` declarations are anonymous (`use@…`) and distinct.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` covers:
  - top-level, impl-level and mod-level item macros as `macro@<12 hex>`
  - the generic impl name `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`
  - expression macros inside function bodies being excluded

**Minor gaps, not enough to fail**
- There is no test for an empty ABI string (`extern "" {}`).
- There is no test for a generic trait path such as `impl From<X> for Y`.
- No test shows a separate `src/local.rs` file with no cross-file resolution. `mod[external]` only demonstrates the absence of resolution, and the implementation has no cross-file logic.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
